criteria.detail: You have been in care, or looked after, for 3 months or more
Your home postcode is in a low-participation neighbourhood: quintile 1 on POLAR4
Your home postcode is in a low-participation neighbourhood: quintile 1 on TUNDRA MSOA

You took part in a recognised outreach or widening participation programme, e.g. Learn with US residential activities for widening participation students, the Learn with US Outreach programme over at least 3 years between Year 9 and 13 (or at least 3 Learn with US activities), or other programmes or mentoring projects with at least 3 interactions
Your home postcode is in decile 1 or 2 of the English Index of Multiple Deprivation (their postcode checker calls this IMD quintile 1)
You were eligible for free school meals after the age of 14 (say so in the 'More about you' section of UCAS)
You are estranged from your parents or guardians (under 25 at the start of the course and studying without the support and approval of any parent)

contextual.rulesText: You are assessed as eligible for contextual admissions if you meet one of the listed criteria (two for Medicine BM5 school-leaver entry). A UCAT bursary voucher is a further criterion for Medicine BM5 school-leavers only. Applies to UK-domiciled home-fee applicants for participating undergraduate degrees (almost all degrees); you must also meet the academic criteria in the course entry requirements. The page describes entry in 2027/28.

source.evidence: We will assess you as eligible for contextual admissions if you meet one of the following criteria

programmes.name: University of Southampton and The Sutton Trust Summer School
programmes.provider: University of Southampton (with The Sutton Trust)
programmes.summary: A free 4-day, 3-night residential at Highfield campus with a subject taster, student-life activities and finance guidance; Business and Economics were among the 2026 subject areas.
programmes.whoCanApply: Home UK students in Year 12 in England or Wales at a state-funded, non-fee-paying school or college, studying subjects relevant to the chosen subject area, who meet at least one widening participation criterion (students who are or have been in care only need to meet the age, school and academic requirements).
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Attend, and have always attended, a state-funded non-fee-paying school or college; Year 12 in England or Wales; relevant subjects; and at least one of: first generation to attend university; free school meals at secondary school; a school or college with below-average attainment or low progression to the top third of higher education; a neighbourhood with low progression to higher education and/or high socio-economic deprivation. Meeting more criteria improves your chances. Home UK students only; you must be available for all dates.
benefits: Free accommodation and meals for the 4 days
Train ticket booked for you, or travel reimbursement of up to £100
Taster lecture and group workshop or practical in your subject
Guidance on finance, student maintenance loans and the cost of living
Access to Sutton Trust support and resources (Sutton Trust Online platform and alumni network)
programmes.subjects: Several subject areas; the 2026 list included Business and Economics
programmes.infoNote: Dates are for the 2027 residential. The page is marked 'for reference only' and says applications open in the Autumn Term; the subject list shown on it is for 2026.

source.evidence: From Tuesday 13 to Friday 16 July 2027, you are invited to join us on campus for a 4-day, 3-night programme.

programmes.name: Ignite your Journey
programmes.summary: A sustained support programme for Year 12 and 13 students from groups under-represented in higher education, with online learning, e-mentoring, Q&As and an on-campus event.
programmes.whoCanApply: Home UK students in Year 12 (or equivalent) who live permanently in the UK and meet at least one criterion: 16 to 19 Bursary or similar grant, or free school meals after age 14; in UK local authority care for 3 months or more, or estranged from family; a young carer; POLAR4 or TUNDRA MSOA quintile 1; or the lowest 20% of the Index of Multiple Deprivation.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Must be a home UK student in Year 12 (or equivalent) living permanently in the UK, and meet at least one of the listed criteria. BA Economics is not available through Ignite your Journey (BSc Economics and the other Economics degrees are not on the excluded list).
benefits: Online learning module on university preparation and study skills
Monthly virtual Q&A sessions on applying to university
E-mentoring with a current Southampton student
Transition and Skills event on campus in April of Year 13
Travel bursaries of up to £100 to attend an Autumn Open Day or Applicant Visit Day (where appropriate)
If you complete it you may be eligible for additional admissions consideration, a £1,000 scholarship in your first year, and support to apply for Ignite your Success
programmes.subjects: All subjects except the listed excluded courses (BA Economics, BM6 Medicine and others)

notes: All course details are for 2027 entry (academic year 2027/28); Southampton has not published 2028 entry requirements yet.
No admissions test is mentioned on the Economics course pages. A-level Maths is required for the BSc courses; the BA Economics and BA PPE offers ask for GCSE Maths grade 6 instead.

Related courses not included: Economics MEcon (L101, 4 years, AAB including Maths), Economics and Actuarial Science (L1N3, AAA including Maths), Mathematics, Operational Research, Statistics and Economics (GL12, AAA or AABB including grade A in Maths) and Philosophy and Economics (VL51, AAB plus GCSE Maths grade 6).
Tuition fee is the same £10,050 for these courses; a full year in employment is charged at 20% of the fee and a full year abroad at 15%.
Southampton plans to run the Learn with US Summer School in 2026-27 but has not published details.
The contextual criteria described apply to entry in 2027/28 and Southampton says postcode classifications can change from year to year.
